messages:
nina_peopleops: Quick question — my baby arrived at home yesterday (planned home birth with midwife). The local registrar hasn't issued a birth certificate yet. Can I add the baby to medical/dental now or do I have to wait for the certificate? Also signing up for benefits while SSN is pending.

jess_benefits: Congrats! 389 You can provisionally add a newborn in a home birth situation. We accept a midwife's signed Birth Attestation + hospital or county filing receipt if available. If the state has an online birth registration confirmation, that works too.

nina_peopleops: What exactly should the attestation include?

jess_benefits: Short checklist to upload to the portal:
- Midwife Birth Attestation (signed, with date/time/place)
- Copy of the newborn's footprint or infant record (if the midwife provides)
- Proof of mother's identity (passport/ID)
- Birth registration receipt or confirmation when available
- SSN or SSN application/ITIN docs when available

nina_peopleops: Where do I upload? Can I DM you?

jess_benefits: Use the benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/portal -> Add dependent -> Newborn (home birth). The portal has a specific "Home Birth" upload type. DM only if you need help.

kai_payroll: For payroll: if you add within 60 days of birth we'll backdate coverage to date of birth and process retro deductions/credits across prior pay periods (usually up to 3). If payroll cutoffs hit we may do an off-cycle adjustment on the next pay run.

nina_peopleops: SSN won't be ready for a few weeks. Is that okay?

jess_benefits: Yes. You can upload the SSN application receipt or leave SSN blank and we will create a temporary dependent record. Once you have SSN, upload it in the portal and benefits will finalize. Note: finalize must be done within 120 days to avoid potential reclassification.

tom_legal: Note on documents: if any non-English documents are submitted (e.g., midwife forms from another jurisdiction), we require a certified translation. Also watch state birth registration timelines; in rare cases we may need additional affidavits.

nina_peopleops: Any tip for urgent claims if baby needs care before docs finalize?

jess_benefits: Claims for urgent care are covered if provisional add is in place. Ask the provider to bill using your dependent name; if provider requests insurance ID we can issue a temporary dependent ID while docs are pending. If you hit denials, escalate to benefits@ and tag me.

hrbot: Reminder: Benefits portal uploads submitted after 5pm PT may be processed the next business day. If you need same-day temporary ID, message @jess_benefits.
